meta.blurb: Behind a stuck drawer in an old desk, Iris finds thirty letters written in 1961 and never posted. She takes the train to the seaside town on every envelope. Someone there never forgot, and Iris has unsent words of her own.
meta.bible: Iris Calloway: a furniture restorer in her late twenties, careful and guarded, who keeps a folder of unsent messages; her workshop is in the city and her lease ends in the autumn. Iris's mother: a carpenter's daughter who taught Iris the trade; her small wooden plane is kept. Pia: Iris's sister, who quarrelled with her over their late mother's house on Pell Road two years ago. Mr Fenn: the auctioneer who sold the desk (Lot 212). Ruth Ashby: a clever, upright woman of eighty-four, once a girl of nineteen on holiday; she wrote the letters in 1961 to 1963 and hid them in her desk; she never married and worked for forty years as a librarian. Hester: Ruth's niece, who sold the desk when she cleared Ruth's flat. Eleanor Ashby: Ruth's gentle mother, who told her in 1962 that Daniel's four letters had been sent back. Ruth's father: a stern banker who moved the family to the city in September 1961, sent Daniel's letters back unopened and told Ruth that Daniel had forgotten her. Daniel Marsh: Ruth's first love, a clockmaker's son, now eighty-six, patient and kind; he waited at the station on Saturday the seventh of October 1961 and his four letters came back; he later married Margaret, who has died. Walter Marsh: Daniel's late father, the old clockmaker. Margaret: Daniel's late wife, warm and wise, who knew about Ruth and never minded. Jonah Marsh: Daniel's grandson, about thirty, a clockmaker, shy and warm. Saltmere: a small windswept harbour town with a white lighthouse, a harbour wall and a village hall. Quay Street: where Marsh and Son clockmakers stands. Marsh and Son: the clock shop. Mrs Dunmore: who keeps the guesthouse on the hill. Harbour View: the care home with a rose garden, two hours' drive from Saltmere. Mr Pascoe: the landlord of the empty shop on Quay Street. The oak desk: has a hidden space behind a stuck drawer, with letters tied with a blue ribbon, the ribbon Ruth wore at the dance in 1961. Ruth and Daniel met in August 1961 when her watch stopped, danced under paper lanterns in the village hall and had three weeks together before her family left on the seventh of September; they promised to meet on the eleven o'clock train on Saturday the seventh of October. Mr Whitlock: a young banker her father brought to dinner in 1961; Ruth refused him. Daniel's four letters came back unopened and he kept them in a biscuit tin; Ruth read them at last at Harbour View. The last line of Ruth's last letter is: If you ever come looking, I shall be waiting, and I shall not mind that you are late. Ruth moved to a whitewashed cottage in Saltmere in late May and the oak desk stands under her window; her old black fountain pen goes to Iris. Iris takes a shop on Quay Street in the summer; Jonah paints its sign, Calloway, Furniture Restorer. Jonah gave Iris a walnut clock he mended; she posts a letter to him from a red post box on her last night in the city. Months and days are named as in the text, from March to late summer. Voice and tone: tender, quiet and hopeful, a gentle love story about saying things out loud, with a happy ending.

beats.scene: Iris bends over a battered oak desk in lamplight
beats.summary: On a cold March evening Iris Calloway begins work on a battered oak desk.

beats.scene: A workshop of clamps, chisels and tins of wax
beats.summary: Iris's workshop and her trade as a furniture restorer show how careful and alone she is.

beats.scene: An auctioneer's hammer falls in a draughty saleroom
beats.summary: Iris remembers buying the desk cheaply at Mr Fenn's auction because nobody else wanted it.

beats.scene: Brass handles and a faint scent of lavender on old oak
beats.summary: Iris studies the desk's drawers and handles and notices one drawer that will not budge.

beats.scene: Iris coaxes a stuck drawer free with a thin blade
beats.summary: Iris spends half an hour working the stuck drawer loose.

beats.scene: Iris's hand reaches into a shallow dark space behind the drawer
beats.summary: She notices the space behind the drawer is too shallow and reaches inside.

beats.scene: A bundle of envelopes tied with a faded blue ribbon
beats.summary: She finds more than thirty letters to Daniel Marsh in Saltmere, none ever posted.

beats.scene: Iris holds an unstamped envelope, unsure whether to open it
beats.summary: Iris hesitates over reading private letters, then unfolds the first.

beats.scene: Thin paper in slanting handwriting, ink faded to weak tea
beats.summary: The first letter, dated the ninth of October 1961, begins Dear Daniel, I will never send this.

beats.scene: The workshop clock shows midnight while Iris reads on
beats.summary: Iris reads on past midnight, drawn into a stranger's summer.

beats.scene: A train arrives in a salt wind beside a grey harbour
beats.summary: Ruth's letters go back to July 1961, when her family arrives in Saltmere for the summer while her father waits for a new post.

beats.scene: A stern banker reads a newspaper on the terrace of a tall grey house
beats.summary: Her father sets rules for everything, and Ruth walks the harbour alone for two bored weeks.

beats.scene: Ruth studies a stopped wristwatch outside a window crowded with clocks
beats.summary: In mid-August her watch stops and she goes into Marsh and Son on Quay Street.

beats.scene: A young man in shirtsleeves opens a watch with tiny tools
beats.summary: Daniel mends the watch, refuses payment and invites her to Saturday's dance.

beats.scene: Ruth ties a blue ribbon in her hair before a spotted mirror
beats.summary: Ruth slips out of the house on Saturday evening wearing a blue ribbon.

beats.scene: Paper lanterns hang across a village hall as couples waltz
beats.summary: At the dance Daniel asks Ruth to dance, and she steps on his foot.

beats.scene: Two young people laugh together in the open doorway of a lantern-lit hall
beats.summary: They laugh about the foot and talk until the band packs up.

beats.scene: Two figures walk along a harbour wall towards a white lighthouse
beats.summary: Daniel walks Ruth home the long way and tells her the lighthouse lamp has never failed.

beats.scene: Iris sets a thin page down beside a cold cup of tea
beats.summary: Near two in the morning Iris realises she is smiling over a stranger's happiness.

beats.scene: A girl lies awake in an attic bed with the window open
beats.summary: That night Ruth lies awake, still hearing the waltz, sure that something has begun.

beats.scene: Daniel shows Ruth shelves of ticking clocks in his father's workshop
beats.summary: Daniel takes Ruth up to the Marsh and Son workshop, where his father Walter nods a quiet welcome.

beats.scene: Daniel's hands guide Ruth's as she winds a heavy brass clock
beats.summary: Daniel teaches Ruth how a clock works and says a clock is patience made into a machine.

beats.scene: A small blue rowing boat circles in green water near a lighthouse
beats.summary: They borrow a boat and row out beyond the harbour wall, and Ruth takes the oars.

beats.scene: Ruth and Daniel eat sandwiches on the harbour wall among gulls
beats.summary: On the harbour wall Daniel dreams of the shop, and Ruth says she only knows what she does not want.

beats.scene: A tired woman in a lamplit hall smiles at her barefoot daughter
beats.summary: Ruth's mother sees her come home late each evening and says nothing, only smiles.

beats.scene: Rain runs down a window as two young people read in a clock shop
beats.summary: On a wet afternoon Daniel reads her a poem and Ruth admits she longs to go to university.

beats.scene: A stern man in a hall holds a telegram, his daughter stands still
beats.summary: Ruth's father announces his new post, the leaving date, and that she must not see the clockmaker's boy.

beats.scene: Two figures hold hands at the foot of a white lighthouse at dusk
beats.summary: On the last evening Ruth tells Daniel at the lighthouse, and he promises to write every week.

beats.scene: Ruth writes an address on a ticket and Daniel folds it into his pocket
beats.summary: They promise to meet on the eleven o'clock train on Saturday the seventh of October.

beats.scene: A packed car leaves a grey house while a girl looks back
beats.summary: On the seventh of September the Ashbys drive away and Ruth watches the lighthouse shrink.

beats.scene: A tall grey city house with iron railings and a dark hall
beats.summary: In the city Ruth's father fills her days with a typing and bookkeeping course.

beats.scene: Ruth stands at her father's study door while he reads the newspaper
beats.summary: Ruth asks to visit Saltmere for one day, and her father says Daniel will have forgotten her by Christmas.

beats.scene: A mantel clock strikes eleven in a stranger's drawing room
beats.summary: On the seventh of October Ruth is sent to take tea with a cousin and imagines Daniel on the platform.

beats.scene: Ruth writes by lamplight at a small oak desk
beats.summary: On Monday night Ruth writes her first letter to Daniel at the desk her father bought her for her studies.

beats.scene: A drawer pulled out of an oak desk reveals a hollow space
beats.summary: The drawer sticks, and Ruth discovers the hidden space behind it, big enough for letters.

beats.scene: Ruth stands in a post office queue holding an addressed envelope
beats.summary: Ruth walks to the post office with the letter but leaves without buying a stamp.

beats.scene: Ruth waits in a dark hall as letters fall on the mat
beats.summary: Every morning Ruth waits for the post, nothing comes for her, and in November she writes a second letter.

beats.scene: A young banker talks across a dinner table while Ruth looks away
beats.summary: Her father invites a young banker, Mr Whitlock, to dinner; Ruth says she prefers letters.

beats.scene: Snow lies on a red pillar box as a girl holds a card
beats.summary: At Christmas Ruth holds a card over the post box slot and takes it home again.

beats.scene: Ruth ties a bundle of letters with a blue ribbon at midnight
beats.summary: On New Year's Eve Ruth ties her letters with the blue ribbon and hides them behind the drawer.

beats.scene: Ruth shelves books in a small public library in spring light
beats.summary: In spring 1962 Ruth takes a library job against her father's wishes and keeps writing a letter every month.

beats.scene: A tired woman weeps at a kitchen table beside a cold kettle
beats.summary: Ruth's mother finally admits that her father sent Daniel's four letters back unopened.

beats.scene: Ruth stands outside a study door with her hand raised to knock
beats.summary: Ruth cannot bring herself to confront her father and goes back to bed without a sound.

beats.scene: Ruth bends over a letter by lamplight, her face tense
beats.summary: Ruth fears Daniel believes she sent his letters back herself, and the waiting grows into a wall.

beats.scene: Ruth sets down a pile of returned books beside a library window
beats.summary: In winter 1963 a friend writes that Daniel is walking out with a girl named Margaret.

beats.scene: Ruth writes by a grey spring window and ties a page into a bundle
beats.summary: In spring 1963 Ruth writes her last letter, admitting she was too frightened to post any.

beats.scene: Thin paper spotted with old tears lies in Iris's hands
beats.summary: Iris reads the last letter twice and is moved by its plain, brave final line.

beats.scene: Iris sits on the floor of the workshop as grey dawn lights the window
beats.summary: At dawn Iris realises she is no better than Ruth at saying what she feels.

beats.scene: Iris opens a folder on her phone in the grey light
beats.summary: Iris opens her secret folder of drafts, dozens of messages never sent.

beats.scene: A message headed Pia sits at the bottom of a long list
beats.summary: The oldest draft is to her sister Pia, written two years ago after a quarrel.

beats.scene: Iris reads a long list of drafts at her bench with coffee
beats.summary: Iris reads every draft in her folder and sees how brave they are and how each was abandoned.

beats.scene: Two women stand among half-packed boxes in a narrow hall
beats.summary: Two years ago, after their mother's funeral, Iris and Pia quarrelled in the house on Pell Road.

beats.scene: Two sisters face each other across a kitchen full of boxes
beats.summary: Pia wanted to sell and Iris wanted to keep, and each said things that could not be taken back.

beats.scene: A worn wooden plane rests on a workbench beside a mug
beats.summary: Iris's mother, a carpenter's daughter, taught her to love wood, and Iris still misses her.

beats.scene: Iris asleep on an old sofa with her phone on her chest
beats.summary: Iris starts a new message to Pia, cannot finish it and sleeps for three hours.

beats.scene: Iris types Saltmere into a laptop at her bench
beats.summary: At noon Iris searches for Saltmere and finds a plain website for Marsh and Son.

beats.scene: Iris paces the workshop with a phone at her ear
beats.summary: Iris rings the shop's number, and it rings fifteen times with no answer.

beats.scene: Iris weighs a bundle of letters with a stamp in her other hand
beats.summary: Iris decides the letters must be delivered by hand, not posted.

beats.scene: A creased auctioneer's card in Iris's dusty apron pocket
beats.summary: Iris finds Mr Fenn's card and telephones him about the desk.

beats.scene: A notepad with a name in capital letters beside a telephone
beats.summary: Mr Fenn says the desk came from Miss Ruth Ashby's flat and promises to ask her niece.

beats.scene: Iris looks at a bundle of letters beside a telephone
beats.summary: Mr Fenn says Ruth's niece is away, and Iris decides to take the letters to Saltmere herself.

beats.scene: Iris sits alone in a cold carriage as a city blurs past
beats.summary: Early the next morning Iris takes the first train with the letters wrapped in her scarf.

beats.scene: An old woman in a green coat knits opposite Iris on a train
beats.summary: An old woman says nobody visits Saltmere in March except for love or for funerals.

beats.scene: The old woman looks up from her knitting at Iris, smiling
beats.summary: The woman advises Iris not to wait for the right words, and Iris thinks of her drafts.

beats.scene: A grey sea shines beside the railway and a lighthouse stands far off
beats.summary: The train reaches the coast, and Iris first sees the white lighthouse.

beats.scene: A tiny station with one platform, a bench and a stopped clock
beats.summary: Iris steps off at Saltmere station, where Daniel once waited for a train.

beats.scene: A steep lane of slate roofs runs down to the sea
beats.summary: Iris walks down the hill, smelling salt and seaweed, past a ginger cat.

beats.scene: Fishing boats rock in a harbour below a long stone wall and lighthouse
beats.summary: She reaches the harbour, which looks exactly as the letters described it.

beats.scene: A faded green shopfront on Quay Street crowded with clocks
beats.summary: Iris finds Marsh and Son on Quay Street and stands outside, trying to feel brave.

beats.scene: A brass bell rings above a door as a tall young man looks up
beats.summary: Iris enters the shop and a tall young clockmaker looks up and does not smile.

beats.scene: A young man lifts a lens from his eye behind a clock-shop counter
beats.summary: Jonah asks if he can help, and Iris asks for Daniel Marsh.

beats.scene: Jonah studies Iris with a wary frown among ticking clocks
beats.summary: Jonah is wary: strangers have called on his grandfather before, and not all were honest.

beats.scene: Old envelopes fan out across a glass shop counter
beats.summary: Iris unwraps her scarf and lays the unposted letters on the counter.

beats.scene: Jonah bends over an envelope, a line between his eyebrows
beats.summary: Jonah reads the address, says Daniel is his grandfather, and has never heard of Ruth Ashby.

beats.scene: Iris talks earnestly across the counter, her hands trembling
beats.summary: Iris tells him everything: the auction, the drawer, the letters and the waltz.

beats.scene: Jonah turns a door sign to Closed and fills a dented kettle
beats.summary: Jonah closes the shop in the middle of the day and makes tea.

beats.scene: A photograph of a laughing woman holding up a trout stands by the till
beats.summary: Jonah says his grandmother Margaret died six years ago and Daniel has grown quiet.

beats.scene: Jonah turns a chipped mug in his hands and remembers
beats.summary: Jonah recalls his grandfather once telling him about a girl who trod on his foot at a dance.

beats.scene: Two figures walk along a windy harbour with a scarf-wrapped bundle
beats.summary: Jonah locks the shop and walks Iris along the harbour, talking about clocks.

beats.scene: An old man in a patched coat throws crusts to gulls on a wall
beats.summary: At the end of the harbour wall they see Daniel feeding the gulls.

beats.scene: An old man in a patched coat turns to greet his grandson
beats.summary: Jonah calls out, and Daniel turns, thin and kind-eyed.

beats.scene: Daniel shakes Iris's hand with old-fashioned courtesy
beats.summary: Daniel greets Iris warmly and teases Jonah for closing the shop.

beats.scene: An old man sits suddenly on a stone wall, a crust falling
beats.summary: Iris says the name Ruth Ashby, and Daniel sits down shaken.

beats.scene: An old man stares at the sea as gulls wheel above him
beats.summary: After a long silence Daniel asks how she knows the name, and Iris explains about the desk.

beats.scene: Daniel sits on a bench in the shelter of a lighthouse wall
beats.summary: On a bench out of the wind Daniel begins to tell the story of 1961.

beats.scene: A young man in his best jacket waits on an empty platform
beats.summary: On the seventh of October Daniel waited at the station in his best jacket for three trains.

beats.scene: Four unopened envelopes stamped Return to Sender lie in a biscuit tin
beats.summary: Daniel's four letters came back unopened, and he thought Ruth had changed her mind.

beats.scene: Iris lays a thin letter in Daniel's open hands
beats.summary: Iris gives him the first letter, and Daniel reads it aloud.

beats.scene: An old man weeps with his grandson's arm around him
beats.summary: Daniel's voice breaks at the line about the clock striking eleven, and Jonah holds him.

beats.scene: Daniel holds Iris's hands as the sun sets over the sea
beats.summary: Daniel asks whether Ruth is alive, and Iris promises to find out.

beats.scene: A large woman in a flowered apron opens a blue guesthouse door
beats.summary: There is no train until morning, so Jonah takes Iris to Mrs Dunmore's guesthouse.

beats.scene: Two people sit on a harbour wall eating fish and chips as gulls watch
beats.summary: At dusk Jonah and Iris eat fish and chips on the wall, and a gull steals a chip.

beats.scene: Jonah and Iris talk side by side on the wall with chips
beats.summary: They talk about their trades: his grandfather's workshop, her mother's lessons.

beats.scene: A lighthouse beam sweeps across dark water, boats and a stone wall
beats.summary: The lighthouse lamp comes on, and Jonah says it has never failed.

beats.scene: Iris lies awake in a narrow room under the roof, window open
beats.summary: Iris lies awake listening to the sea and thinking of Pia and of Jonah.

beats.scene: Trays of tiny wheels and springs lie under lamps in a long workshop
beats.summary: Next morning Jonah shows Iris the workshop above the shop.

beats.scene: Jonah holds a hair-fine spring in tweezers up to a window
beats.summary: Jonah says clockwork is mostly waiting, and Iris says wood is the same.

beats.scene: A walnut clock case with a long crack lies on a bench
beats.summary: Iris offers to mend a customer's cracked clock case.

beats.scene: Two hands meet on a clamp over a glued crack
beats.summary: Their hands touch on the clamp as they tighten it, and they both pause.

beats.scene: Iris shows Jonah a phone screen crowded with unsent messages
beats.summary: While the glue dries Iris tells Jonah about her drafts, and he says to send the one to Pia.

beats.scene: Iris listens, wide-eyed, with a phone at her ear in the workshop
beats.summary: Mr Fenn telephones: Ruth Ashby is alive, eighty-four and sharp as a tack.

beats.scene: Iris writes an address in black pen across the back of her hand
beats.summary: Ruth lives at Harbour View, two hours away, and Iris writes the address on her hand.

beats.scene: An old man lays down a potato knife at a kitchen table
beats.summary: Iris and Jonah run to Daniel's cottage and tell him, and he sits very still.

beats.scene: A photograph of a laughing woman in a straw hat on a mantelpiece
beats.summary: Daniel says Margaret always knew about Ruth and never minded.

beats.scene: A dented biscuit tin of four sealed envelopes held against an old man's chest
beats.summary: Daniel fears being a stranger to Ruth and fetches his four returned letters.

beats.scene: A young man ties a tie for his grandfather in a hallway
beats.summary: Next morning Jonah ties Daniel's tie and leaves a note on the shop door.

beats.scene: A battered blue van drives along a bright coast road with three people
beats.summary: The three drive to Harbour View along the coast.

beats.scene: An old man taps a biscuit tin and hums with his eyes closed
beats.summary: On the road Daniel hums the waltz from the dance.

beats.scene: A long white house on a hill above the sea, with bare rose beds
beats.summary: They reach Harbour View, with its rose garden just breaking into leaf.

beats.scene: An old man sits on a garden bench, shaking hand on a tin
beats.summary: Halfway up the path Daniel stops, too nervous to go in.

beats.scene: A nurse points down a corridor lined with watercolours of the sea
beats.summary: Iris goes in alone and a kind nurse sends her to the sun room.

beats.scene: A small white-haired woman reads by a sunny window
beats.summary: Iris finds Ruth Ashby in the sun room, small and upright, with a library book on her knee.

beats.scene: Iris holds out a bundle of letters tied in a scarf
beats.summary: Iris asks if she is Miss Ruth Ashby and holds out the letters.

beats.scene: An old woman presses a faded blue ribbon to her cheek
beats.summary: Ruth sees the blue ribbon and laughs and cries at the same time.

beats.scene: An old woman clasps her hands as she tells of a stuck drawer
beats.summary: Ruth says the drawer stuck the day she hid the last letter, and her niece sold the desk by mistake.

beats.scene: An old woman asks a question, her fingers tight on a ribbon
beats.summary: Ruth asks whether Iris knows what became of Daniel Marsh.

beats.scene: Iris kneels and holds an old woman's hand
beats.summary: Iris says Daniel is in the garden, and Ruth smooths her hair, trembling.

beats.scene: An old man stands in a doorway turning a cap in his hands
beats.summary: Iris brings Daniel in, and he stops at the sun room doorway.

beats.scene: Two old people laugh across a sunny room
beats.summary: Ruth tells Daniel he is late, and they both laugh and cry.

beats.scene: Two old people sit hand in hand as one reads a thin page
beats.summary: Ruth reads her last letter aloud, and Daniel answers its last line.

beats.scene: Two figures stand in a bare rose garden looking at a lit window
beats.summary: In the garden Jonah says he has never seen his grandfather look so young.

beats.scene: Jonah asks a question gently as Iris holds her phone
beats.summary: Jonah asks what her own letter is waiting for, and Iris takes out her phone.

beats.scene: Iris deletes a long draft and types three plain lines
beats.summary: Iris cuts her two-year-old draft to three plain lines for Pia.

beats.scene: A thumb hovers above a send arrow among rose bushes
beats.summary: After a long moment Iris presses send.

beats.scene: Two people walk in circles around bare rose beds in the wind
beats.summary: Jonah distracts her with a story about a clock that ran backwards.

beats.scene: A phone screen lights up with a short reply
beats.summary: Pia answers at once, saying she has waited two years and Mum would be glad.

beats.scene: Iris laughs and sobs as a handkerchief is held out
beats.summary: Iris laughs and cries, and Jonah gives her a clean handkerchief.

beats.scene: Iris walks alone at the end of a garden, phone to ear
beats.summary: Iris rings Pia, and the sisters say sorry and laugh together.

beats.scene: An old woman holds a sealed envelope in a bright sun room
beats.summary: Ruth explains why she never posted her letters, and Daniel says he never forgot her.

beats.scene: An old woman turns to a young woman with a request
beats.summary: Ruth says she is glad Daniel married Margaret and asks Iris to finish the desk and bring it to her.

beats.scene: An old woman lifts a hand to wave beside a clock on the wall
beats.summary: Visiting time ends, and Daniel promises to come back every Saturday.

beats.scene: A blue van drives along a dark coast road, headlights sweeping
beats.summary: On the drive home Daniel falls asleep against the window, smiling.

beats.scene: A young man drives with his eyes ahead, a woman beside him
beats.summary: Jonah asks Iris to dinner in the city, and she says she could be persuaded.

beats.scene: An old man holds a young woman's face under a streetlamp
beats.summary: At his gate Daniel kisses Iris's forehead and thanks her three times.

beats.scene: A lighthouse beam sweeps over two people at a blue guesthouse door
beats.summary: Jonah walks Iris up the hill, and they say a shy goodnight.

beats.scene: A young man in the wind on a tiny platform as a train arrives
beats.summary: Next morning Jonah sees Iris off at the station and promises to ring every evening.

beats.scene: A woman leans her forehead on a train window, smiling to herself
beats.summary: On the train Iris realises she has been smiling since the harbour.

beats.scene: A scraper strips old polish from a golden oak desk under a lamp
beats.summary: Back in her workshop Iris begins stripping the old polish from the desk.

beats.scene: A phone rings on a workbench beside a tin of wax at seven o'clock
beats.summary: Every evening at seven Jonah rings, and they talk about everything.

beats.scene: A hand slides a waxed drawer smoothly in and out of an oak desk
beats.summary: Iris first mends the secret drawer so that it will never stick again.

beats.scene: Two small letters scratched into the wood beneath an oak drawer
beats.summary: Iris finds the initials R and A scratched under a drawer, beside a half-rubbed heart.

beats.scene: A pale ring of old ink on the stripped top of an oak desk
beats.summary: A ring where Ruth's ink bottle stood shows on the desktop, and Iris decides to keep it.

beats.scene: Iris holds a phone to her ear at the workbench in lamplight
beats.summary: Jonah tells her Ruth has read Daniel's four old letters at last.

beats.scene: A woman in a good coat stands at a workshop door with cake
beats.summary: On the second Saturday Pia visits the workshop with a lemon cake.

beats.scene: Two sisters sit on an old sofa with tea and cake
beats.summary: The sisters chat, and then Pia says she wants to talk about the house.

beats.scene: Two sisters hold hands over empty plates, both crying
beats.summary: Pia admits her fear about money, and Iris admits she could not bear to lose Mum again.

beats.scene: Two women stand by a kitchen table in a quiet workshop
beats.summary: They agree to sell the house, keep their mother's chair, tools and table, and say goodbye together.

beats.scene: Pia runs a hand along a half-restored oak desk beneath a lamp
beats.summary: Pia hears the whole story of the desk and wants to meet Ruth, Daniel and the clockmaker.

beats.scene: A soft cloth polishes honey-coloured oak under a workshop lamp
beats.summary: In the third week Iris waxes the finished desk until it glows.

beats.scene: A wet young man in a doorway holds a cloth-wrapped parcel
beats.summary: Jonah arrives in the rain with a small walnut clock he has repaired.

beats.scene: A small walnut clock ticks above a workbench in lamplight
beats.summary: Jonah hangs the walnut clock on her workshop wall, and the room sounds alive.

beats.scene: A young man holds out a mended clock, ears pink
beats.summary: Jonah says it was silent for forty years and he mended its case as she taught him.

beats.scene: Iris laughs at her stained overalls, holding a hairbrush
beats.summary: Jonah asks her to dinner, and Iris changes her clothes.

beats.scene: A small restaurant glows with candles in wine bottles on a rainy corner
beats.summary: They go to a warm corner restaurant and slowly stop being shy.

beats.scene: Jonah slides a creased envelope across a tablecloth between the salt and a candle
beats.summary: Over dinner Jonah gives Iris a letter he almost never sent.

beats.scene: Iris reads a single sheet by candlelight, her hand at her mouth
beats.summary: Jonah's letter says she makes him braver than he has ever been.

beats.scene: Iris kisses Jonah beside a candlelit table as diners watch
beats.summary: Iris stands and kisses Jonah in front of the whole restaurant.

beats.scene: A waiter sets down a pudding with two spoons and one candle
beats.summary: The room applauds, and a waiter brings a pudding with the compliments of the house.

beats.scene: Two people share one small umbrella on a rainy street
beats.summary: They walk home in the rain, and Jonah asks her to take the desk to Ruth on Saturday.

beats.scene: Iris stands at a workshop door with a key, looking up at Jonah
beats.summary: At her door Iris tells him she is glad he came and means to say so often.

beats.scene: Three people lower a blanket-wrapped desk down a narrow stair
beats.summary: On Saturday Iris, Pia and Jonah wrap the desk in blankets and load it into the borrowed van.

beats.scene: A white van drives along a bright coast road beside the sea
beats.summary: They drive two hours to Harbour View with the desk strapped in the back.

beats.scene: An old man waits at a gate holding yellow daffodils
beats.summary: Daniel waits at the gate of Harbour View, having come by the early train.
